beats.text: At first, Sita was afraid. Was this Ravana in disguise again?
Hanuman climbed down, bowed, and dropped Rama's ring into her lap. She saw Rama's name on it and wept with joy, as if she had seen Rama himself.
He told her how Rama could not sleep or eat, and spoke her name every night.
He offered to carry her back right then, on his back, across the ocean.
'No,' said Sita. 'Rama must come and rescue me himself, for his honor. And I will not willingly touch another man.'
She told him a secret only Rama knew: how Rama once punished a crow that hurt her with a single blade of grass, made into a divine weapon.
She gave him her hair jewel, the Choodamani, as proof. 'Tell Rama I am waiting. I can live one month more.'
